claims.text: Role in delayed puberty: boys w ⍉pubertal signs by 14 y may get a 4–6-mo course of ↓dose testosterone (eg, cypionate, enanthate) once a mo;
claims.quote: If boys show no sign of pubertal development by age 14 years, they may be given a 4- to 6-month course of low-dose testosterone (eg, cypionate, enanthate) once per month.
claims.locator: Treatment of Delayed Puberty › Hormone therapy

claims.text: these ↓doses induce puberty w some virilization and don't jeopardize adult height potential;
claims.quote: These low doses induce puberty with some degree of virilization and do not jeopardize adult height potential.
claims.locator: Treatment of Delayed Puberty › Hormone therapy

claims.text: testosterone enanthate (or cypionate/propionate) 50–100 mg IM monthly × 3–6 mo = enough to start pubertal development.
claims.quote: Testosterone enanthate injection (or cypionate/propionate) at a dosage of 50 to 100 mg IM monthly for 3 to 6 months is sufficient to initiate pubertal development.

claims.text: Peds safety (testosterone enanthate label): in children, androgens may accelerate bone maturation w.o compensatory linear growth, compromising adult height; the younger the child, the greater the risk;
claims.quote: In children, androgen treatment may accelerate bone maturation without producing compensatory gain in linear growth. This adverse effect may result in compromised adult stature. The younger the child the greater the risk of compromising final mature height.

claims.text: check skeletal maturation (hand and wrist XR) every six months.
claims.quote: Skeletal maturation must be monitored every six months by an X-ray of the hand and wrist
